header.stance: 前端反彈較強，長端實質利率仍高

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 油價回落帶動短債反彈，實質殖利率仍居高檔

油價回落，John Williams也表示，若核心通膨降溫，Fed仍可耐心等待，美債週四反彈。2年期殖利率下降5個基點至4.16%，30年期卻僅下降1個基點至5.05%。前兩個交易日的跌勢獲得部分修復，但長天期借款成本並未同幅緩解。

10年期殖利率下降2個基點，完全來自通膨補償降低，實質殖利率維持2.31%。布蘭特原油下跌2.20%，荷莫茲航運嚴重受阻與偏高煉油利潤卻仍威脅燃料價格。失業救濟金資料也呈現兩面：裁員仍少，持續請領人數卻上升。

長債標售以2007年以來最高的得標殖利率找到買盤，且優於發行前交易水準。股市上漲、波動率降低，上市信用債基金小幅走高。不過，借款人與融資結構的差異依然明顯：$350億AI晶片融資的部分債務準備進入可交易市場，另一些企業則付出極高的再融資利率，或尋求債權人協助重整。

## 通膨補償下降支撐美債，就業資料顯示再就業放慢

2年期殖利率下降5個基點至4.16%，5年期下降4個基點至4.27%，10年期下降2個基點至4.54%，30年期下降1個基點至5.05%。前端反彈較強，使2年與10年期利差擴大3個基點至38，2年與30年期利差擴大4個基點至89。各天期殖利率仍較一週前高，累計升幅分別為2、4、5及7個基點；這次牛市趨陡，對長端累積跌勢的修復較有限。

10年期損益兩平通膨率下降2個基點至2.23%，實質殖利率維持2.31%。5年期實質殖利率下降1個基點至1.99%，7、20及30年期則維持2.14%、2.66%及2.86%。油價降低了通膨補償，卻未明顯改變投資人對較長天期要求的實質報酬。

截至7月4日的一週，初領失業救濟金減少2,000人至21.5萬人，四週平均降至218,750人。截至6月27日的一週，持續請領增加8,000人至181.4萬人，四週平均升至180.8萬人，受保失業率維持1.2%。企業並未大量裁員，但已失業的人似乎需要更久才能找到下一份工作。

Williams指出，AI相關需求若持續推升通膨，貨幣政策可能需要回應。他也提出一項可以耐心等待的具體條件：下半年核心PCE月增率若維持0.2%，便符合通膨持續朝Fed 2%目標下降的路徑；若更快，就代表通膨更具黏性。這番說法延伸了週三會議紀錄中的條件式選擇，並非承諾按照市場提前的時間表升息。

### 長債在高殖利率吸引較佳投標

30年期增額標售的得標殖利率為5.058%，低於截止前發行前交易的5.061%。雖是2007年以來最高得標殖利率，結果仍優於預期，幫助美債殖利率自盤中高點回落；新券稍早一度交易在5.095%。繼本週3年與10年期標售成功之後，殖利率讓利再次吸引投資人。

這股需求卻未帶動長端實質殖利率下降。政府發債仍與AI基礎設施所需的大額企業融資競爭資金，在5%以上順利完成標售，不等於長期資本變便宜。30年期僅反彈1個基點，遠小於2年期的幅度。

財政部另發行約$1,000億28天期與$950億56天期國庫券，最高利率分別為3.630%及3.635%，均於7月14日交割。投標倍數分別為2.64及2.95，8週期的投資人參與較強：間接投標人取得74.57%、交易商20.98%，4週期則分別為56.61%與38.77%；直接投標人的比例分別為4.46%及4.62%。

次級市場最短天期表現不一。4週期殖利率上升6個基點至3.69%，6週期下降2個基點至3.68%，8週期維持3.71%。3個月以上則大致隨政策敏感的美債天期下行：13、17及26週期分別下降4、3及4個基點，至3.78%、3.86%及3.92%，一年期下降3個基點至4.02%。

Fed於美東16:30公布的每週資產負債表顯示，截至7月8日的一週，平均準備金餘額增加$1,320億至$3.099兆；財政部一般帳戶平均減少$1,062億至$7,741億，附賣回餘額則增加$40億至$3,488億。數字支持銀行體系流動性充足的判斷，但公布時，當天大部分漲勢已經發生。

## AI融資即將進入交易市場，不同風險各有價格

Apollo與Blackstone安排的$350億Broadcom-Anthropic融資，預計未來幾個月隨資金撥付，陸續有部分債務可供交易。明年初約$150億可能進入市場，投資人預期到2027年夏季，累計動用約$240億。分批撥款將讓這筆既有私募逐步進入更廣泛的交易市場。

借款的特殊目的公司購買Google與Broadcom開發的晶片，再租給Anthropic，最大幾個優先順位部分的付款由Broadcom提供支持。融資隨晶片到位，在一年多期間分約16次撥付；已動用的債務可於144A市場交易，買方包括保險公司、共同基金等合格投資人。更廣泛的機構將能取得這類設備融資曝險，實際交易也會呈現部位轉手的難易程度。

QTS的Project Magnolia則補充了先前$20億融資的資產細節：擔保品為四州共12座已完工資料中心，全數出租給三家投資級大型雲端業者。營運資產提供已簽約的現金流，這次再融資也將用於向股東分配資金。組合包含$10億定期貸款，利差225至250個基點、發行價格99至99.5，以及另$10億擔保債務。QTS在4月已為Microsoft支持的專案發行$46億投資級債券。

TeraWulf準備為肯塔基州園區籌措約$35億貸款與高收益債。這家由比特幣挖礦轉型的公司，已與Anthropic簽署20年租約，預計產生約$190億收入；先前曾於12月發行$13億、10月發行$32億垃圾債，新方案將首次進入槓桿貸款市場。長約提高收入可見度，但建設中資產尚未建立QTS完工資料中心已有的營運現金流。

AI以外，收購與再融資交易也持續推進。Barclays準備約$8.75億債務，支應英國航太供應商Senior的收購，包括兩筆優先擔保定期融資及循環額度。Well Health則尋求私募C$1.5億、5年期高收益債，用於償還今年到期的可轉債及一般企業用途。

### 現金吃緊的企業付出更高再融資代價

Shapoorji Pallonji在旗下Goswami Infratech債務兩度展延後，啟動計畫中的INR2,550億、約$27億再融資。其中約INR1,500億的3年期本幣零息債，預期殖利率18.95%，既有投資人約19.05%；Deutsche Bank可能投入約$4億。交易處理了迫近的到期壓力，代價卻十分高昂。

Vestel Elektronik聘請Houlihan Lokey，評估2029年5月到期$5億美元債的處理選項，同時重新協商本地銀行貸款。Fitch將評等下調兩級至CCC-、認為資本結構難以維持後，債券下跌約7美分至面額52%。銀行貸款占債務約75%，因此在收入承壓、人工、原料與物流成本上升侵蝕現金流之際，解方必須協調本地銀行與國際債券持有人。

Aston Martin方面，週三報導的債權人小組持有逾半數優先擔保票據，$10.5億2029年美元債當天跌約4美分至面額72%。第一季收入成長仍無法避免£6,550萬稅前虧損，淨負債達£14.6億。債權人準備聯合協商之際，現金需求已讓公司的迴旋空間十分有限。

ION Platform則顯示，保留更多現金可以支持債價修復。第二季收入成長5.1%、EBITDA成長14.3%，向母公司的分配由$3.14億降至$5,300萬，上半年已買回約$2.5億債務。淨槓桿由7.49倍降至6.53倍，帶動€6億2032年債券上漲3.5美分至78.6。淨負債仍有$110億，進一步改善仍須靠獲利與持續保留現金。

LQD上漲0.04%、HYG上漲0.11%、JNK上漲0.10%。大盤小幅走高之下，個別發行人的處境差距很大：AI債務準備開始交易、有企業付出高價延後到期，有企業尋求重整，也有債券因獲利改善而反彈。

## 歐債反彈，日本與英國仍面對長端融資難題

油價回落帶動歐洲殖利率下降。德國2年期在前一天上升12個基點後，回落2個基點至2.68%；英國各天期最多下降3個基點。德國5月出口增加0.9%至€1,379億，進口下降2.5%至€1,188億，經調整貿易順差由€147億擴大至€191億。

ECB緊縮定價卻幾乎未鬆動。交換市場反映9月升息機率90%，年底前再一次升息的機率接近一半。核心通膨動能與偏高成品油成本仍讓央行需要謹慎；債券反彈相對週三跌勢不大，並非重新轉向降息預期。

日本央行維持九個地區的整體景氣評估不變。各地雖有部分弱點，仍都形容經濟復甦或回升，就業與所得改善，企業投資則增加或已處高檔。關東甲信越新增與中東相關的疲弱描述。報告支持進一步正常化，也承認進口能源除了推升價格，還可能傷害活動。

日本5年期標售投標倍數3.43，高於12個月平均3.35；平均與最低得標價格差由6月0.06縮至0.03。結果公布後期貨仍走弱，5年期殖利率維持近2%，10年期約2.9%、為1996年以來最高。投標改善，卻未解決財政支出、弱勢日圓，以及日本央行升息是否趕得上通膨的疑慮。

英國投資人則質疑，債務管理局能否完成本年度計畫中的£224億長天期發債。前三個月尚未發行任何剩餘期限至少15年的債券。發債授權允許改變天期組合與配售方式，可減輕短期長端壓力，但也會反映需求波動對政府籌資的限制。

歐洲共同借款方面，德國與法國質疑西班牙提出、將更多國家債務集中至歐盟發行的構想；Christine Lagarde則主張建立可與美債競爭的歐洲資產。提案預想五年內形成約€5兆債務存量，每年為政府最多節省€250億利息。統一市場可能改善流動性與儲備資產吸引力，但政治共識與責任如何分配仍待解決。

## 韓國以低利差取得歐元資金，區域政策路徑仍分歧

韓國發行€17億外匯穩定債，包括€7億3年期、利差為中間交換利率加10個基點，以及€10億7年期、加28個基點。兩券均較指引收窄約4個基點，創該主權最低利差。此次比慣常下半年時程提早發行，可補充先前支撐韓元所動用的外匯存底，也為其他韓國借款人建立基準。

韓國央行總裁Shin Hyun Song向國會表示，通膨高於目標、經濟成長改善及金融穩定風險，意味著需要在適當時機升息，下一次會議為7月16日。報告指出半導體帶動成長，首爾都會區房價加速、槓桿投資增加；油價下降仍不足以抵銷內需轉強的影響。相對地，馬來西亞因通膨受控、匯率較強，得以維持隔夜政策利率2.75%。

印尼較高殖利率幫助穩定匯率後，6月外資流入本幣主權債的規模創13個月新高。週三2年與10年期殖利率分別為7.29%及7.31%，提供可觀的持有收益，但油價下降對抑制進口通膨、降低央行再次升息需要仍十分重要。荷莫茲若再受阻，能源進口國將尤其不利。

截至6月底，中國用於將地方隱性債務轉為正式政府債券的人民幣6兆元額度，已使用約94%，其中上半年發行逾人民幣1.62兆元。置換可降低昂貴地方融資平台債務的償付成本、提高透明度，卻不會消除底層的公共負擔。內需疲弱與支出限制，也壓縮了經濟效益。

塞內加爾的壓力更大。未揭露負債使先前IMF計畫中斷後，政治陣營又對新計畫是否應調整債務產生分歧，提高延後到期、重新安排償債時程的可能。美元債對美債利差達1,548個基點，為非洲主權最高；沉重支付壓力延續至2028年，政府依賴本地與區域市場融資。Citigroup不認為即將違約，但警告，若沒有結構改革，展期或延付可能只是將重整推遲，也延後重返國際市場。

美債殖利率降低、美元指數下跌0.11%至100.94，帶動EMB上漲0.18%至$95.96。共同環境改善，卻無法消除韓國低利差外部融資、印尼能源敏感度與塞內加爾債務協商之間的差別。

## 科技股上漲，偏高成品油利潤限制原油降價效益

S&P 500上漲0.81%，Nasdaq 100上漲1.62%，半導體上漲3.06%，VIX下降6.27%至15.84。科技股支撐風險偏好，但AI投資規模也正是Williams擔心需求及通膨持續的原因。

WTI在週三大漲後下跌1.96%至$72.08，布蘭特下跌2.20%至$76.30，兩者仍高於一週前。汽油裂解價差接近每桶$57，說明原油變便宜，不代表成品油成本已正常化：荷莫茲交通嚴重受阻，俄羅斯煉油設施又遭攻擊，供應仍受限制。

名目殖利率下降、美元轉弱，帶動黃金上漲1.47%至$4,130.60。金價與股票同漲、波動率下降，較符合保留部分地緣避險，而非全面撤離風險資產。長端實質殖利率未降、成品油利潤仍高，也限制了當日油價跌勢能帶來的金融緩解。

## 通膨細項與燃料庫存，決定反彈能否延續

6月CPI與實質所得將於7月14日美東08:30公布，PPI為7月15日08:30，零售銷售及初領失業救濟金為7月16日08:30。核心與服務通膨、生產成本傳導及零售控制組，將為Williams的條件式政策看法提供新證據。再就業轉慢之際，除了偏低的初領人數，持續請領也值得留意。

財政部將於7月13日美東11:30合計發行$1,710億13週及26週期國庫券，7月14日11:30再發行$950億42天期，7月16日交割。日本7月14日約¥7,000億20年期標售，則把需求考驗延伸至長天期。投資人參與及標售後交易，將顯示本週強勁投標能否承接下一波供給。

EIA石油庫存報告於7月15日美東10:30公布，天然氣庫存為7月16日10:30。汽油、蒸餾油庫存、煉廠運作與裂解價差，將顯示原油降價能否傳到消費者；天然氣注入量則可判斷庫存是否仍保有相對五年平均的緩衝。若成品油持續去庫存、或煉油受限，即使原油價格穩定，通膨壓力仍可能延續。

overall_summary.headline: 油價回落、短債反彈，長期融資成本仍難下降
overall_summary.session_narrative:
油價下降，Williams也表示核心通膨若降溫，Fed仍可耐心等待，帶動美債反彈。2年期殖利率下降5個基點至4.16%，10年期下降2個基點至4.54%，完全來自通膨補償降低。失業救濟金資料則顯示裁員少，但持續請領人數增加。

30年期增額標售得標殖利率5.058%，優於發行前交易，卻仍是2007年以來最高，長端實質殖利率也未降。信用市場方面，$350億Broadcom-Anthropic融資的部分債務準備開始交易；TeraWulf尋求建設資金，Shapoorji Pallonji再融資利率接近19%，ION債券則因獲利改善、向母公司分配減少而反彈。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Oil Relief Lifts Short Treasuries, but Real Yields Hold Firm

Treasuries recovered Thursday as oil retreated and John Williams left room for the Fed to remain patient if underlying inflation cooled. Two-year yields fell 5 basis points to 4.16%, while the 30-year declined just 1 to 5.05%. The rally reversed part of the previous two sessions' losses without bringing comparable relief to long-duration borrowing costs.

At 10 years, the 2-basis-point yield decline came entirely through lower inflation compensation; real yield held at 2.31%. Brent fell 2.20%, but severe disruption to Hormuz shipping and high refining margins still threatened fuel prices. Jobless claims also presented a mixed picture: layoffs remained low, while more people continued to collect benefits.

The long-bond auction found buyers at the highest award yield since 2007, clearing below pre-sale trading. Equities rallied, volatility eased and listed credit gained modestly. Beneath that improvement, financing continued to divide by borrower and structure. Portions of a $35 billion AI-chip package were preparing to enter the tradable market, while other borrowers paid exceptionally high refinancing yields or sought creditor-led repair.

## Lower Breakevens Drive the Rally as Claims Show Slower Re-employment

The two-year yield fell 5 basis points to 4.16%, five years declined 4 to 4.27%, 10 years eased 2 to 4.54% and 30 years slipped 1 to 5.05%. The stronger front-end recovery widened 2s10s by 3 basis points to 38 and 2s30s by 4 to 89. Yields were still higher over the week, with gains of 2, 4, 5 and 7 basis points respectively. The day's bull steepening repaired less of the accumulated losses farther out the curve.

Ten-year breakeven inflation fell 2 basis points to 2.23%, leaving real yield unchanged at 2.31%. Five-year real yield eased 1 basis point to 1.99%, but seven, 20 and 30 years held at 2.14%, 2.66% and 2.86%. Lower oil reduced inflation compensation without materially changing the real return investors required at longer maturities.

Initial claims fell 2,000 to 215,000 in the week ended July 4, and their four-week average declined to 218,750. Continuing claims increased 8,000 to 1.814 million for the week ended June 27, lifting the average to 1.808 million; the insured unemployment rate stayed at 1.2%. Employers were not laying off workers in large numbers, but those already out of work appeared to be taking longer to find another job.

Williams identified sustained AI-related demand as an inflation risk that monetary policy might need to address. He also offered a concrete condition for patience: monthly core PCE increases of 0.2% in the second half would fit continued disinflation toward the Fed's 2% target. A faster pace would suggest more persistence. His comments developed the conditional choices in Wednesday's minutes rather than committing the committee to the earlier hike priced by markets.

### Long-Bond Bidding Improves at a High Yield

The 30-year reopening was awarded at 5.058%, below the 5.061% pre-auction yield shortly before the deadline. It was the highest award yield since 2007, but the result was stronger than expected and helped Treasuries retreat from session yield highs. The new bonds had traded as high as 5.095% earlier. After the week's successful three- and 10-year sales, investors again responded to yield concession.

That demand did not lower long-end real yields. Government issuance still competes with the substantial corporate borrowing needed for AI infrastructure, and a successful sale at more than 5% is not the same as cheaper long-term capital. The 30-year's 1-basis-point rally was considerably smaller than the two-year's gain.

Treasury also sold about $100 billion of 28-day bills at a 3.630% high rate and $95 billion of 56-day bills at 3.635%, both settling July 14. Coverage was 2.64 and 2.95 respectively. The eight-week sale had stronger investor participation: indirect bidders took 74.57% and dealers 20.98%, compared with 56.61% and 38.77% at four weeks. Direct allocations were 4.46% and 4.62% respectively.

Secondary bill moves were mixed at the shortest maturities. Four weeks rose 6 basis points to 3.69%, six weeks fell 2 to 3.68% and eight weeks held at 3.71%. From three months onward, yields generally fell with the policy-sensitive Treasury sector: 13, 17 and 26 weeks declined 4, 3 and 4 basis points to 3.78%, 3.86% and 3.92%, while one year fell 3 to 4.02%.

The Fed's weekly balance-sheet release, published at 16:30 ET, showed average reserve balances up $132.0 billion to $3.099 trillion in the week ended July 8. The average Treasury General Account fell $106.2 billion to $774.1 billion, while reverse repos rose $4.0 billion to $348.8 billion. The figures supported a liquid banking backdrop, but were released after most of the day's rally had occurred.

## AI Financing Moves Toward Trading as Borrowers Pay for Different Risks

Parts of the $35 billion Broadcom-Anthropic financing arranged by Apollo and Blackstone were expected to become tradable as funds were drawn over the coming months. About $15 billion could be available for trading by early next year, with investors expecting roughly $24 billion drawn by summer 2027. The delayed funding would gradually bring the existing private placement to a wider market.

A special-purpose vehicle buys chips developed by Google and Broadcom and leases them to Anthropic. Broadcom backstops payments on the largest senior portions. Funding is divided into about 16 releases over more than a year as chips become available; drawn debt can then trade in the 144A market among qualified investors, including insurers and mutual funds. The transition will give a wider buyer base access to equipment-linked credit and reveal how readily those positions change hands.

Additional detail on QTS's Project Magnolia placed its previously reported $2 billion financing against 12 completed data centers across four states. Fully leased to three investment-grade hyperscalers, the assets provide contracted operating cash flow, while the refinancing also funds a sponsor distribution. The package consists of a $1 billion term loan at a 225–250-basis-point margin and a 99–99.5 issue price, plus $1 billion of other secured debt. QTS had already sold $4.6 billion of investment-grade bonds in April for a Microsoft-backed project.

TeraWulf was preparing roughly $3.5 billion of loans and high-yield bonds for a Kentucky campus. The former bitcoin miner had signed a 20-year Anthropic lease expected to generate about $19 billion of revenue. It had already issued $1.3 billion of junk debt in December and $3.2 billion in October; the new plan would mark its first move into leveraged loans. Contracted revenue improves visibility, but the construction-stage asset has yet to demonstrate the operating cash flow available at QTS's completed properties.

Acquisition and refinancing pipelines remained active outside AI. Barclays was preparing about $875 million of debt for the takeover of British aerospace supplier Senior, including two senior secured term facilities and a revolver. Well Health sought C$150 million of five-year high-yield bonds in a private placement to repay a convertible due this year and fund general purposes.

### Refinancing Costs Rise Where Cash Is Scarce

Shapoorji Pallonji began a planned INR255 billion, or $2.7 billion, refinancing after twice extending debt at Goswami Infratech. Roughly INR150 billion of three-year zero-coupon local bonds were expected to yield 18.95%, with existing investors near 19.05%. Deutsche Bank could invest about $400 million. The transaction addressed an approaching maturity, but at a very high cost.

Vestel Elektronik hired Houlihan Lokey to examine options for its $500 million dollar bond due May 2029 while renegotiating local bank loans. The bond fell about 7 cents to 52 after Fitch cut the issuer two notches to CCC- and described the capital structure as unsustainable. Bank loans make up around 75% of debt, requiring coordination across domestic lenders and Eurobond holders as weak revenue and higher labor, material and logistics costs erode cash generation.

At Aston Martin, the creditor group reported Wednesday held more than half the senior secured notes. Its $1.05 billion 2029 dollar bond had fallen about 4 cents to 72 that day. First-quarter revenue growth had not prevented a £65.5 million pretax loss or net debt of £1.46 billion. Those cash demands left little room for the company as creditors prepared to negotiate together.

ION Platform showed how improved cash retention could support a recovery. Second-quarter revenue rose 5.1%, EBITDA increased 14.3% and distributions to its parent fell to $53 million from $314 million. About $250 million of debt had been repurchased in the first half. The €600 million 2032 bond gained 3.5 cents to 78.6 as net leverage declined to 6.53 times from 7.49. Net debt was still $11 billion, leaving further gains dependent on earnings and continued cash retention.

LQD rose 0.04%, HYG 0.11% and JNK 0.10%. Those small broad gains accompanied very different issuer outcomes: tradable AI credit, expensive maturity extensions, adviser-led restructuring and an earnings-backed bond rebound.

## European Bonds Recover, but Japan and the UK Face Long-End Funding Questions

European yields fell as oil eased. Two-year Bunds declined 2 basis points to 2.68% after rising 12 the previous day, and gilts recovered by as much as 3 basis points across the curve. German May exports grew 0.9% to €137.9 billion while imports fell 2.5% to €118.8 billion, widening the adjusted trade surplus to €19.1 billion from €14.7 billion.

The price of ECB tightening barely loosened: swaps put a September increase at 90%, with the probability of another year-end move close to even. Core inflation momentum and high refined-fuel costs still warranted caution. The recovery in bonds was modest relative to Wednesday's selloff, not a return to an easing outlook.

The BOJ left all nine regional assessments unchanged. Every region reported recovery or pickup, despite some weakness, with employment and incomes improving and business investment rising or already high. Kanto-Koshinetsu added a qualifier about Middle East-related weakness. The report supported further normalization while recognizing that imported energy can hurt activity as well as raise prices.

Japan's five-year auction drew 3.43 bid-to-cover, above the 12-month average of 3.35. The gap between average and lowest accepted prices narrowed to 0.03 from June's 0.06. Futures nevertheless weakened afterward; the five-year yield remained near 2% and the 10-year around 2.9%, its highest since 1996. Improved bidding had not resolved concerns over fiscal spending, a weak yen and whether BOJ tightening was keeping up with inflation.

British investors questioned whether the DMO could complete its planned £22.4 billion of long-dated issuance for the fiscal year. No bond with at least 15 years remaining had been sold during the first three months. The remit permits changes in maturity mix and distribution method, which could reduce near-term long-end pressure but would also reflect the constraints imposed by volatile demand.

At the European level, Germany and France questioned Spain's proposal to centralize more national borrowing at the EU. Christine Lagarde argued for a European asset able to compete with Treasuries. The proposal envisaged a debt stock near €5 trillion within five years and annual government interest savings of up to €25 billion. A unified market could improve liquidity and reserve appeal, but the political agreement and distribution of obligations remained unresolved.

## Korea Secures Tight Euro Funding as Local Policy Paths Diverge

South Korea sold €1.7 billion of foreign-exchange stabilization notes: €700 million at three years, 10 basis points over mid-swaps, and €1 billion at seven years, 28 basis points over. Both priced about 4 basis points through guidance and at record-tight sovereign spreads. Issuing ahead of its usual second-half schedule replenished reserves used to support the won and set a benchmark for Korean borrowers.

Bank of Korea Governor Shin Hyun Song told lawmakers that inflation above target, stronger growth and financial-stability risks would require an increase at an appropriate time. The next meeting was July 16. His report pointed to semiconductor-led growth, faster Greater Seoul house prices and leverage-fueled investment; lower oil alone was not enough to offset stronger domestic demand. Malaysia, by contrast, held its overnight policy rate at 2.75%, with contained inflation and a firmer currency allowing patience.

Indonesia attracted a 13-month high in foreign inflows to rupiah sovereign bonds in June after higher yields helped stabilize the currency. Two- and 10-year yields were 7.29% and 7.31% on Wednesday. That carry offered support, but lower oil remained important to containing imported inflation and the need for further Bank Indonesia tightening. Renewed Hormuz disruption would be particularly unwelcome for energy importers.

China had used about 94% of its CNY6 trillion allowance to replace hidden local-government liabilities with official bonds by the end of June, following more than CNY1.62 trillion of issuance in the first half. The conversion reduces servicing costs on expensive LGFV debt and improves transparency without eliminating the underlying public obligation. Weak domestic demand and spending constraints still limit its economic benefit.

Senegal faced much greater financing pressure. Political disagreement over debt modification for a new IMF program increased the prospect of maturity reprofiling after undisclosed liabilities derailed the prior program. Its dollar-bond spread was 1,548 basis points over Treasuries, the widest among African sovereign issuers, with heavy payments through 2028 and reliance on domestic and regional markets. Citigroup did not see imminent default, but warned that extensions or deferrals without structural reform could postpone a later restructuring and delay renewed international access.

EMB rose 0.18% to $95.96 as Treasury yields fell and DXY slipped 0.11% to 100.94. The common backdrop improved, though it could not remove the differences between Korea's tight external pricing, Indonesia's energy sensitivity and Senegal's debt negotiations.

## Technology Rallies While Fuel Margins Limit Oil Relief

The S&P 500 gained 0.81%, Nasdaq 100 rose 1.62% and semiconductors advanced 3.06%. VIX fell 6.27% to 15.84. The technology rally supported risk appetite, even as the scale of AI investment remained central to Williams' concerns about persistent demand and inflation.

WTI fell 1.96% to $72.08 and Brent declined 2.20% to $76.30 after Wednesday's surge. Both remained higher over the week. Gasoline crack spreads near $57 a barrel showed why cheaper crude did not yet mean normal fuel costs: Hormuz traffic was severely impaired, and attacks on Russian refining capacity added another constraint.

Gold rose 1.47% to $4,130.60 as nominal yields declined and the dollar softened. It gained alongside equities and lower volatility, consistent with some residual geopolitical hedging rather than a broad flight from risk. Flat long-end real yields and high refined-product margins still limited how much financial relief could be inferred from the day's oil decline.

## Inflation Detail and Fuel Inventories Will Determine Whether Relief Lasts

June CPI and real earnings arrive July 14 at 08:30 ET, followed by PPI July 15 at 08:30 and retail sales and initial claims July 16 at 08:30. Core and services inflation, producer-cost pass-through and the retail control group will add evidence to Williams' conditional outlook. Continuing claims also warrant attention alongside low initial filings, given the signs of slower re-employment.

Treasury sells a combined $171 billion of 13- and 26-week bills July 13 at 11:30 ET, then $95 billion of 42-day bills July 14 at 11:30, ahead of July 16 settlement. Japan's roughly ¥700 billion 20-year auction July 14 will extend the test to longer duration. Investor participation and post-auction trading will show whether the week's strong bidding survives the next wave of supply.

The EIA petroleum report is due July 15 at 10:30 ET and natural-gas storage July 16 at 10:30. Gasoline and distillate inventories, refinery operations and crack spreads will show whether lower crude reaches consumers. Gas injections will also indicate whether stocks retain their five-year inventory cushion. Continued product draws or refining constraints could preserve inflation pressure even if headline crude stabilizes.
